The digitised speech, the only sampled sound in this part and presumably what the credits call 'speech by B.-Jones': a one-bit sample player under the BASIC ROM, run with BASIC banked out and interrupts off. The first word at $A090 is the length counted from $A090 ($09F0, end $AA80); the pointer $FB/$FC reads at offset 2, so the samples are $A092-$AA81 plus one bit of $AA82. Each byte is shifted out from bit 7: a 1 sets the SID volume ($D418) to 15, a 0 sets it to 0, with padding NOPs so each bit takes about 100 to 130 cycles: some 9,400 bits a second, 2.2 seconds in all (measured by running it in the kit's 6502 simulator). Ends with $D418 = $18.
A 1 bit: volume 15, then a run of NOPs so the two bit paths take roughly the same time.
A 0 bit: volume 0, then speech_pad.
Three NOPs and RTS, the timing pad used by speech_bit0 and after each bit's end check.
Length of the speech data counted from this word: $09F0, so speech_play stops when its pointer reaches $AA80.

The speech samples, one bit per sample, most significant bit first, played at about 9,400 samples a second by speech_play: $A092-$A491, the first 1,024 bytes. A run of 707 zero bytes ($A453-$A715, about 0.6 s of silence) splits the speech into two phrases.
Speech samples, $A492-$A891 (continued from speech_data).
Speech samples, $A892-$AA82, the end of the speech (the last played bit is bit 7 of $AA82).

Hires bitmap fragment, 2,560 bytes laid out as eight 320-byte character rows: pieces of a picture with the words 'A VIEW TO A KILL' in large letters across rows 3-4. Only the unreachable dead_copy ($C500) refers to it (it would copy $B000-$B9FF to the bank-1 bitmap at $6000); the intro never shows it. Rows 0-2 here.
title_fragment continued, $B400-$B7FF: the 'A VIEW TO A KILL' lettering and the shapes above it.
title_fragment, last part, $B800-$B9FF.

The white dots that open a Bond film: all sprites on, sprites 0 and 1 white with shape pointer $20 ($0800, a filled circle), both at X 24, Y $87. Five times: sprite 1 moves right one pixel per dot_delay, 66 pixels, then sprite 0 jumps 66 pixels to catch it up, setting the X high bits in $D010 when the sums pass 255. Blocking, about four seconds.
Busy-wait of 7 x 255 inner loops (about 9,000 cycles), the speed of rolling_dots.

Switches the screen to multicolour bitmap mode ($D011 bit 5, $D016 bit 4), fills the colour matrix $03E0-$07DF with $02 (pixel pairs %01 black, %10 red) and colour RAM $D800-$DBFF with 0 (pairs %11 black, so the picture starts invisible), moves sprites 0 and 1 to X $110, Y $10 (above the visible area), sets 38 columns with X scroll 7, falls into bitmap_base ($C0E0).
Second half of bitmap_setup: bitmap at $2000 ($D018 bit 3), blood pointer $A3/$A4 = $2000 and blood line count $A7 = $C0 (192 pixel lines) for blood_step, then runs rolling_dots ($C000) to its end.

Reveals the gun-barrel picture from the right: writes white (1) into colour RAM one column at a time, column 39 down to column 11 (29 columns), rows 0-22, with a delay of 16 x 255 loops between columns. Pixel pairs %11 turn from black to white.

Called by the IRQ each time the fine X scroll wraps: clears $42 so scroll_copy prepares the other buffer, and makes CIA 2 show VIC bank 1 ($4000, the $6000 bitmap) when $41 = 1, bank 0 ($0000, the $2000 bitmap) otherwise. The colour matrix and sprite pointers exist in both banks ($0400/$07F8 and $4400/$47F8).
Entry of swap_bank that always selects VIC bank 1 ($DD00 bits 0-1 = %10) and clears $42; also called by speech_and_fade once the bitmap has been cleared.
Saves the 64 bytes of music-driver state $C600-$C63F to $9F00 before the gunshot and the speech.
Copies the 64 saved bytes at $9F00 back to $C600 and sets $D418 back to $1F (filter mode low-pass, volume 15), so the tune carries on where it stopped.

Bond walks in from the right, turns and fires (called by barrel_step every second frame). Advances the frame index $AD (0-7). While the step count $02 is not 0: moves sprites 0-2 one pixel left (clearing $D010 when X borrows past 0) and every fourth call ($AC) shows walk frame $AD from walk_frames and DEC $02. When $02 is 0: every fourth call shows turn frame $33 from turn_frames, and when $33 reaches 2 fires the gunshot (gunshot, $CABC). Shape pointers go to both screens, $07F8 and $47F8.

Prepares the walking Bond: sprites 0-2 black, hires, unexpanded, stacked at Y $7E, $92, $A6 (head, body, legs) and X $130 (off the right edge, $D010 = $FF), shapes $22/$23/$24, only sprites 0-2 enabled. Walk step count $02 = $22 (34 frames), animation frame $AD = 7, turn index $33 = 0. The $D01B writes ($FF then 0) end with the sprites in front of the picture.
Shape pointers for Bond's eight walk frames, three tables of eight read by bond_step with the frame index $AD: $C2E0 head ($22, $25 ... $37), $C2E8 body ($23 ... $38), $C2F0 legs ($24 ... $39).
walk_frames' second table: body shapes $23, $26, $29, $2C, $2F, $32, $35, $38 for sprite 1.
walk_frames' third table: leg shapes $24, $27, $2A, $2D, $30, $33, $36, $39 for sprite 2.
Shape pointers for the two turn frames, three tables of two read by bond_step with $33: $C2F8 head ($3A, $3D), $C2FA body ($3B, $3E), $C2FC legs ($3C, $3F).
turn_frames' body table: $3B, $3E for sprite 1.
turn_frames' legs table: $3C, $3F for sprite 2.

After the gun barrel: shows VIC bank 0, runs speech_and_fade ($CA80), sets up the credits screen (credits_setup, $CB50), then builds the Domark logo out of sprites 2-7: shapes $40-$45 (bank 1, $5000-$517F), multicolour with $D026 white, sprite colour red ($02), sprites 0 and 1 white; start positions from logo_start_pos ($C3C0), all eight sprites on, $D010 = $C0; then logo_assemble ($C430).

One step of the logo pieces: for each position register of sprites 2-7 ($D004-$D00F, Y = 4 to 15) reads logo_dir ($C3F0): 0 leaves it, bit 7 set moves it one pixel back (logo_dec), otherwise one pixel on (logo_inc). For the Y registers, bit 6 holds the move back while the step count $02 is $6B or more (the first 22 of the 128 steps).

Start positions for the Domark logo, copied to $D000-$D00F by after_barrel (X, Y for sprites 0-7): sprites 0 and 1 at 0,0 (the sparkles, placed later), sprite 2 at 0,0, 3 at 0,$FF, 4 at $98,0, 5 at $98,$FF, 6 at $30,0 and 7 at $30,$FF, 6 and 7 with the X high bit ($D010 = $C0): the six pieces start at the top and bottom edges, left, centre and right, and logo_move brings them together.
For logo_inc, indexed by sprite register (0-15): the $D010 bit of that register's sprite ($01, $01, $02, $02 ... $80, $80), ORed in when an X position passes 255.
For logo_dec, indexed by sprite register: the inverse masks ($FE, $FE, $FD ... $7F, $7F) that clear a sprite's $D010 bit when its X drops below 0.

Movement codes for logo_move, one per sprite register $D000-$D00F: 0 still, 1 add one each step, $80 subtract one, $C0 subtract one but only after the first 22 steps. Sprites 2-7: X +1, +1, 0, 0, -1, -1 and Y +1, -1 (late), +1, -1 (late), +1, -1 (late): in 128 steps the left pieces move 128 pixels right, the right ones 128 left, the top pieces 128 down and the bottom ones 106 up.
Adds 1 to sprite register $D000+Y; when it wraps to 0 on an X register, sets that sprite's $D010 high bit from logo_msb_set.
Subtracts 1 from sprite register $D000+Y; when it wraps to $FF on an X register, clears that sprite's $D010 high bit with logo_msb_clear.

Domark logo: 128 steps ($02 from $80) of logo_move with a delay of $20 x 255 loops each, bringing the six pieces in from the top and bottom edges of the screen. Then prints the title lines (title_print, $90A0), puts two white sparkle sprites (0 and 1, shapes $46/$47) at $7E,$75 and $B1,$9F, and enters sparkle_loop.

The intro's final loop: after a delay of $48 x 255, steps both sparkle shapes through $46, $47, $48. While no credit line has been printed ($8D = 0) it counts $02FD down from $10 and, on 0, switches the IRQ to mode 2 (the credits scroll). When 84 lines have been printed ($8D = $54) it puts the KERNAL's $EA31 back in $0314 and sets the SID volume to 0: the scroll and the music stop, and the sparkles go on for ever. There is no exit: this part never loads another.
Unreachable fragment after sparkle_loop: DEX/BNE into the middle of the JMP at $C4B8, DEY/BNE, JMP $C4B3. Left over from an earlier version of the loop.

Unreachable (no caller): copies $B000-$B9FF to $6000-$69FF and then loops on itself at $C525 for ever. The LDA $01 / AND #$FE at its start is discarded (never stored), so with BASIC banked in it would copy BASIC ROM. A leftover.

Selects 24 text rows ($D011 bit 3 clear) and sets the fine Y scroll counter $02FF to 7. Its LDA $D011 reads bit 7 as the current raster line's bit 8, not as the compare bit credits_setup wrote, so the compare line goes back to $0F0/$0F8 only if this runs while the raster is on lines 0-255; on lines 256-311 no raster interrupt would come again (open question).

Every fifth frame in IRQ mode 2: moves the fine Y scroll ($D011 bits 0-2, counter $02FF) up one pixel; when it passes 0 it goes back to 7, sets $02FB and calls credits_newline ($9050) to move the text up one row and print the next line.

Intro set-up, reached from copy_tune_start. Calls tune_init ($C640), clears the IRQ mode $0313 and the credit-line counter $8D, enables the VIC raster interrupt (only) at line $F8, points the KERNAL's IRQ vector $0314 at irq_handler ($CC00), CLI, and jumps to copy_banks ($CA00). The CIA 1 timer interrupt stays on and still reaches the KERNAL through irq_handler.

Unreachable (no caller in the image): black border and background, then a three-level delay loop counting $02E0/$02E1/$02E2 down from $20/$FF/$FF, about 19 million cycles. A leftover like the other dead fragments at $C4BB and $C500.
Music driver state (the 64 bytes $C600-$C63F are saved and restored around the gunshot and the speech). $C600-$C602: attack/decay for voices 1-3, set by tune_init to $2E, $18, $1F.
Voice 2 attack/decay ($18).
Voice 3 attack/decay ($1F).
$C603-$C605: control register value for each voice when a note starts, $41 (pulse wave, gate on).
Voice 2 control value ($41).
Voice 3 control value ($41).
$C606-$C608: pulse width high byte for each voice, $0C, $0D, $0C.
Voice 2 pulse width high ($0D).
Voice 3 pulse width high ($0C).
Tempo phase, 0 or 1: with 0 the next step comes after three frames, with 1 after two (tune_tick). $00 at the hand-over.
Frames since the last note step, counted by tune_tick; $01 at the hand-over.
$C60B-$C60D: low bytes of the three voices' note pointers; $C60E-$C610 the high bytes.
Voice 2 note pointer, low byte ($EC at the start).
Voice 3 note pointer, low byte ($F1 at the start).
$C60E-$C610: high bytes of the voices' note pointers, $E0, $E1, $E5 at the start of the tune.
Voice 2 note pointer, high byte ($E1 at the start).
Voice 3 note pointer, high byte ($E5 at the start).
$C611-$C613: duration counters, steps left of each voice's current note; 8 at the start.
Voice 2 duration counter.
Voice 3 duration counter.
$C614-$C616: each voice's current low frequency byte, the base that tune_vibrato adds its offset to.
Work byte of voice_step: the low frequency byte just read.
Work byte: the pulse width high byte of the voice being stepped.
Work byte: the control value of the voice being stepped.
Work byte: the attack/decay of the voice being stepped.
Work byte: the duration counter of the voice being stepped, counted down by voice_step.
tune_read's copy of the processor port $01 while it reads with all RAM banked in.
Index of the voice being stepped (0-2) in tune_step.
$C61E-$C620: vibrato offsets, 0, 4, 8, 12 in turn, per voice; $C621-$C63F are not used but ride along in music_save's block.

Music driver set-up (the same driver sits at the same address in city-hall): per voice attack/decay $2E/$18/$1F ($C600-$C602), control $41 pulse with gate ($C603-$C605), pulse width high $0C/$0D/$0C ($C606-$C608); filter cutoff $0F/$5A, voice 1 through the filter, low-pass with volume 15 ($D415-$D418); falls into tune_restart.
Points the three voices at the start of their note lists, $E000, $E1EC and $E5F1 (copies of $8500, $86EC and $8AF1), and sets each duration counter to 8.

Once per raster interrupt: tune_vibrato, then the tempo divider. $C609 flips between 0 and 1 and $C60A counts frames, so the notes advance after three frames and two frames in turn (20 steps a second on PAL); on each step tune_step ($C6E0), then the end check tune_check_end.
One note step for each voice X = 0-2: copies the voice's pointer to $D9/$DA and its settings to the work bytes $C618-$C61B, calls voice_step, and stores back the counter and the advanced pointer.

Counts the voice's duration down; at 0 plays its next note from ($D9): gate off, attack/decay, frequency high then low (the low byte kept in $C614,X for the vibrato), pulse width high, control with gate, and the new duration from the note's third byte; the pointer moves on three bytes. Sustain/release is never written.
Reads the note byte ($D9),Y with the processor port $01 at 0, all RAM, so the note lists under the KERNAL ROM are visible; restores $01 from $C61C.
When voice 1's pointer reaches $E1EC, the end of its list, jumps to tune_restart: the whole tune starts over, whatever voices 2 and 3 are doing. Voice 3 has then played up to $E962 ($8E62).
Every frame, for each voice: adds 4 (modulo 16) to its offset $C61E,X and writes the note's low frequency byte plus that offset to the SID, a small repeating rise in pitch on every note.
SID register offsets of the three voices, 0, 7, 14, used by voice_step and tune_vibrato.
The gun-barrel opening, first half: bitmap_setup ($C074, which also plays the rolling dots), bond_setup ($C280), then JMP barrel_scroll ($CB00).

Every second frame in IRQ mode 1. While $3F is not 0: steps the fine X scroll ($D016 bits 0-2) down by one pixel, and when it passes 0 sets it back to 7 and calls swap_bank; then bond_step ($C200) and DEC $3F. Once $3F is 0 it runs blood_step instead.
barrel_step's store: new fine scroll $AE into $D016, bond_step, DEC $3F. (The seven bytes before it, $C82B-$C831, are unreachable junk.)

The blood running down the barrel, one pixel line per call (every second frame, 192 calls while $A7 counts down): EORs with $55 the 40 bitmap bytes of one pixel line at ($A3), which turns white pixel pairs (%11, colour RAM) into red (%10, the matrix's low nibble $2) and black %00 into black %01. Steps $A3/$A4 to the next pixel line, adding $140 minus 7 at the foot of a character row. Works on the bank-0 bitmap at $2000, the one on show when the scroll ends.

Screen shake after the shot: 58 ($3A) steps, each writing the next fine X scroll value to $D016 (6 down to 0, then up to 7, and back down), with a delay of $30 x 255 loops between steps. The blood keeps running in the IRQ meanwhile.

Copies VIC bank 0 into bank 1 before anything is shown: $0800-$1FFF (sprite shapes and the credits character set) to $4800-$5FFF, and $2000-$3FF0 (the gun-barrel bitmap) to $6000-$7FF0, so both halves of the double-buffered scroll start with the same picture. Then jumps to barrel_sequence ($C800).
One dissolve pass: ANDs every byte of the bank-0 bitmap $2000-$3FF0 with the mask in $C9, and writes the result both back and to the same place in bank 1 ($6000), 31 pages and 240 bytes.

Speech, then the picture dissolves. SEI, a delay of 255 x 255 loops, saves the music state (music_save, $C1B0), banks BASIC out ($01 bit 0 cleared) to reach the player at $A000 under the BASIC ROM, plays the speech (speech_play), banks BASIC back in, restores the music (music_restore), CLI. Then clears the bitmap in five passes of bitmap_mask with masks $FF, $FC, $F0, $C0, $00 (the right-hand pixel pairs of every byte go first) and shows VIC bank 1 (show_bank1).

The shot, called by bond_step inside the IRQ: saves the music state, SEI, a delay, then voice 3 as noise: volume 15, frequency $BAAA, attack/decay $09, sustain/release $05, gate on ($81); a delay of 255 x 255 loops while it sounds; restores the music (music_restore, which also resets $D418 to $1F) and CLI. Music stops for the length of the shot.

Gun-barrel main loop. white_wipe ($C100) reveals the picture, clears the raster high bit, sets the scroll counter $3F = $90 (144 IRQ steps) and $40 = 3, switches the IRQ to mode 1 (INC $0313) at raster line $F0, marks bank 0 shown ($41 = 2, $42 = 0), then repeats scroll_copy ($CD00) and barrel_colour ($CE00) until $3F reaches 0. Then waits until blood_step's pointer high byte $A4 reaches $31 (about 13 character rows of blood), shakes the screen (shake, $C900) and goes on to after_barrel ($C300).

Credits screen: text mode with 24 rows and Y scroll 7 ($D011 = $97), 38 columns, X scroll 7 ($D016 = $C7), credit pointer reset (credits_reset, $9000), colour RAM all white, the screen at $4400-$47FF all spaces; continues into charset_copy. The $97 also sets bit 7 of $D011, the raster compare's bit 8, moving the interrupt line to $1F0, which a PAL screen never reaches; only the read-modify-write in credits_scroll_init puts it back (see there).

Copies the 128-glyph character set $1800-$1BFF to $4800, points $D018 at screen $4400 and characters $4800 (value $12 in VIC bank 1), multicolour off, CIA 2 to bank 1, and credits_scroll_init ($C540). The byte after its RTS starts '$02, STA $0313, RTS' (an LDA #$02 whose opcode the RTS has replaced), so an earlier version started the credits scroll here at once.

Five bytes after charset_copy's RTS: $02, $8D $13 $03, $60, the rest of LDA #$02 / STA $0313 / RTS, the RTS at $CBE7 having replaced the LDA's opcode. In an earlier version charset_copy started the credits scroll (IRQ mode 2) itself; here sparkle_loop does it after the logo.

Interrupt handler, through the KERNAL vector $0314. Acknowledges the raster interrupt; any other source (the CIA 1 timer) goes to the KERNAL's $EA31. On a raster interrupt it dispatches on $0313: 1 goes to irq_mode1 ($CC30, the gun-barrel scroll), 2 to irq_mode2 ($CCD0, the credits scroll), anything else straight to irq_music ($CCF7).
IRQ mode 1: re-arms the raster compare at line $F0 and every second frame ($40 counts 2) calls barrel_step ($C809), then plays the music.

IRQ mode 2: re-arms the raster compare at line $F8 and every fifth frame ($02FE counts 5) calls credits_scroll ($C54E), then plays the music. $02FE is not set before the mode starts: it is 0 at the hand-over, so the first scroll step comes 256 frames (about five seconds) after the mode is switched on.
Common IRQ exit: one tick of the music driver (tune_tick, $C6AB), then pulls Y, X and A as the KERNAL's $FF48 pushed them and returns with RTI.

Main-loop half of the double-buffered horizontal scroll. Does nothing while $42 is set (the hidden buffer is ready). Otherwise shifts the hidden bitmap left by two cells (16 bytes) over 30 pages: with $41 = 2 (bank 0 shown) it copies $6010 onward to $6000 (bank 1) and sets $41 = 1; with $41 = 1 it copies $2010 onward to $2000 (bank 0) and sets $41 = 2; both set $42 = 1. Each row's first two cells move into the end of the row above, so the picture wraps diagonally.
Copy loop of scroll_copy, also called for the bank-0 buffer from $CD49: $1E pages from ($FD) to ($FB), then marks bank 1 as the one to show next ($41 = 1) and the buffer ready ($42 = 1).
scroll_copy's path for $41 = 1: shifts bitmap $2010-$3E0F down to $2000 through scroll_copy_loop, then overrides its $41 with 2 (bank 0 next).

Main-loop colour work during the scroll: when $3F is exactly $42 it whitens colour RAM columns 5-15 of rows 0-23; while $3F is below $3A it whitens columns 0-6 of rows 0-23 (every pass). Together with white_wipe this lets the picture show white as it scrolls in from the right. Returns without work otherwise.
barrel_colour's second case: colour RAM columns 0-6 of rows 0-23 set to white.
